ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, UBO, director and signatory against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the EU consolidated financial sanctions lists including Regulations (EU) No. 269/2014, 833/2014 and 2023/2878; (iii) the French national asset-freeze lists maintained by the Direction Générale du Trésor under Article L.562-2 of the Monetary and Financial Code; (iv) the OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions Lists as required by the correspondent bank for any USD Swift wire; and (v) PEP databases per FATF Recommendation 12 and Article L.561-10 CMF. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by the non-resident corporate shareholder structure, by the 25% UBO threshold, and by the ISIC 2720 'medium-risk enhanced' classification, requiring source-of-wealth documentation, beneficial-ownership chain evidence, ongoing transaction monitoring, and the filing of a déclaration de soupçon to TRACFIN within one business day of any suspicion without tipping off the client.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); availability and conflict screening through the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and the RCS search tools on infogreffe.fr; the name clearance is embedded in the single incorporation filing and is definitively protected upon RCS registration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registered corporate documents must be in French pursuant to Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994 (loi Toubon). The company name must use Latin script; any non-Latin shareholder or brand name must be transliterated into French/Latin alphabet and accompanied by a certified French translation. The corporate legal form suffix 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or the abbreviation 'SAS' must appear immediately after the corporate name. The registered name must be distinctive and must not create confusion with existing RCS trade names or registered trademarks under Articles L.711-2 and L.711-3 of the French Intellectual Property Code.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: France (requires prior authorization from the Direction Générale du Trésor of the Ministry of the Economy)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not issue a standalone name-reservation certificate; the name is cleared through the single incorporation dossier at the INPI Guichet Unique. The dossier and the provisional name hold for a 30-day processing window; inactivity or non-reply to a greffe request for completion causes the draft name to lapse and requires a fresh filing. Upon a name rejection on grounds of confusion, public policy or prohibited tokens: (1) the incorporator must file a rectified dossier at the Guichet Unique, which supersedes the rejection; (2) if the rejection is maintained, a recours gracieux may be addressed to the INPI Director within two months of notification; (3) a refusal issued by the greffier du tribunal de commerce can be contested before the President of the Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of notification under Articles L.123-5-1 and R.123-104 of the Commercial Code; (4) where the conflict is trademark-based, the applicant may negotiate a consent letter or challenge the opposing trademark in the courts; and (5) in all cases a secondary name draft should be substituted before expiry of the 30-day window to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional only. A commercial domiciliation (virtual office) is lawful for the SAS head office for a maximum statutory period of five years under Law No. 2020-768 and Decree No. 2020-1525 of 3 December 2020, and is acceptable for the incorporation stage and for management correspondence. However, for the ISIC 2720 sodium-ion battery-cell manufacturing activity, the ICPE environmental authorization is site-specific under Articles L.512-1 and L.512-7 of the French Environmental Code; no authorization will be issued to a virtual address, so a physical production and storage facility must be secured and declared before the operating licence is granted. The virtual office therefore cannot satisfy the commercial-substance requirements of the industrial permit or of the DREAL inspection regime.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65.0% baseline probability of an unannounced DREAL physical inspection within the first 12 months of operation for an ICPE-classified new-energy battery-cell facility operating under the 'enregistrement' regime (ICPE rubriques 2661 and/or 1630); the likelihood rises above 85.0% if the facility is placed under the 'autorisation environnementale' regime. DREAL inspectors have statutory power of warrantless access during operating hours under Article L.171-1 of the Environmental Code, with no prior notice required.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9, L.227-1 to L.227-20, R.123-1 to R.123-30, and R.227-1 to R.227-2; French Civil Code provisions on contracts and mandates also apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the National Institute of Industrial Property (INPI), with registration in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE) and the relevant Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) maintained by the competent commercial court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online declaration of creation of a company (déclaration de création d'une société) submitted through the Guichet unique, accompanied by executed articles of association and beneficial-owner declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. The articles must state the capital amount. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must generally be fully paid at incorporation. Cash contributions are deposited with an authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations account pending registration; the deposit certificate is then used for release of funds. The stated USD fee is an approximate conversion of the standard RCS registration fee of approximately EUR 37.45 and excludes beneficial-owner filing, legal-notice publication, professional fees, and any sectoral charges.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accept the subscriptions for its issued share capital in accordance with the executed articles of association and the subscription schedule, and that all required cash contributions be deposited with an authorized depositary. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full French address], as stated in the articles. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed President (Président) for the term and authority specified in the articles, and that [name] be appointed General Manager (Directeur général), if applicable. RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to complete all filings, publications, banking formalities, and licensing applications required for registration and commencement of operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm corporate structure and statutory particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders, shareholders, and appointed corporate officers; legal review before submission to the INPI Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS name, registered office, purpose, duration, capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance powers, President, General Manager if any, financial year, and beneficial owners. Verify identity, capacity, sanctions, and non-resident shareholder information.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and business-purpose statement
Officer identity, declaration of non-conviction, and certificate of parentage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies before signature; obtain written confirmation of registered-office eligibility and replace incomplete identity evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of association and appointment instruments. Signatures may be electronic if legally reliable and auditable. Obtain required officer declarations and ensure the corporate purpose covers battery-cell manufacture, storage, testing, import, export, and ancillary activities.
required_dossiers: Optional appointment decision for General Manager
Officer declarations of non-conviction and parentage
Power of attorney for filing representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-execute defective documents, correct signature authority, and document any shareholder ratification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized French bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital-deposit account, provide the executed articles, shareholder and officer identification, subscription schedule, and anti-money-laundering information, and transfer the subscribed cash capital. Obtain the certificate of deposit for filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank KYC queries, provide source-of-funds evidence, correct account-holder mismatches, or use another authorized depositary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal of Legal Notices (journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a statutory formation notice containing the company name, form, capital, registered office, purpose, duration, President, and registration details as applicable. Obtain the publication certificate and retain the invoice.
required_dossiers: Executed articles or verified statutory particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Republish a corrected notice if mandatory particulars are omitted or inaccurate and attach the replacement certificate to the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online declaration of creation, upload the executed articles, capital deposit certificate, publication certificate, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, identity documents, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay applicable filing charges and electronically sign the application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the INPI dashboard, answer requests for regularization within the stated deadline, replace rejected files, and resubmit after correcting formal defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration identifiers and activate banking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI, competent RCS clerk, INSEE, and the authorized bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm issuance of the SIREN, SIRET, APE code, RNE extract, and RCS registration evidence. Deliver the registration extract to the bank, convert the temporary account into an operating account, and release deposited capital.
required_dossiers: Bank mandate and officer authority documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Contact the RCS clerk or INPI support channel for delayed processing; correct any mismatch between declared activity, APE code, and actual business purpose.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-incorporation governance and tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French tax administration, URSSAF, labor authorities, and company statutory auditors where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain mandatory corporate registers and accounting records, establish accounting and payroll systems, register employees with URSSAF, assess statutory-auditor thresholds or group-control obligations, and confirm corporate-tax, VAT, and customs profiles with the tax administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File corrected tax or social declarations, request administrative regularization, and document any late-filing explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The Préfet of the department in which the facility is located, acting through the relevant Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), under the French classified-installations regime (Installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement, or ICPE). The applicable regime must be determined from the ICPE nomenclature, process, substances, storage quantities, and site capacity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Depending on the applicable ICPE classification: environmental authorization (autorisation environnementale) and prefectural operating order; environmental registration (enregistrement); or declaration with receipt (déclaration ICPE avec récépissé). Separate building, planning, water, waste, and product-compliance approvals may also be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, through the competent regional environmental authority and the regional environmental authority (Mission régionale d'autorité environnementale, MRAe), with the Préfet as competent permitting authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not automatically determinable from the ISIC code alone. A full environmental authorization and environmental assessment may be required if the proposed ICPE activities meet the applicable authorization thresholds or other EIA criteria. Registration or declaration may apply below those thresholds, with case-by-case environmental screening where required under Articles L.122-1 and R.122-2 of the French Environmental Code.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the applicable prefectural order, ICPE general prescriptions, Water Framework and French water-police requirements, local wastewater discharge authorization, and applicable EU industrial-emissions and BAT requirements. Control wastewater for pH, suspended solids, COD, metals, electrolytes, and other site-specific pollutants; control VOCs and dust according to permit limits; segregate, characterize, store, track, and transfer hazardous waste through authorized contractors. Battery materials, waste batteries, chemicals, and transport must also comply with Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, REACH, CLP, and French waste-tracking rules. No universal limit applies without the final process and permit classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before construction and operation, obtain applicable planning and building permits, verify structural loads for production equipment and battery storage, and obtain fire-safety review or approval from the competent local authority and fire and rescue service where required. Prepare fire-risk, thermal-runaway, explosion-risk, emergency-response, evacuation, hazardous-material storage, and battery incident procedures. Comply with the French Labour Code, occupational-risk assessment obligations, chemical-agent exposure controls, electrical and machinery safety, ventilation, personal protective equipment, workplace medical arrangements, and mandatory declarations or inspections for regulated pressure, lifting, and fire-protection equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via impots.gouv.fr portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS: obtain SIREN/SIRET via INPI, then register for VAT by filing Form SI/FL through the DGFiP business portal; VAT ID is issued under Article 286 CGI. Foreign entities without permanent establishment must register for VAT via the DGFiP foreign-registration unit (SIE) before making taxable supplies in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (SAS is subject to corporate income tax at 25% standard rate; no pass-through). Territorial scope: worldwide income for established entities, with exemptions for foreign PE income under tax treaties. No tax-exempt zone.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable. France does not recognise check-the-box elections; a SAS is invariably a separate taxable person. Hybrid mismatch elections may only arise as disclosures under Article 205 A CGI and DAC6 for cross-border arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 for goods (franchise en base de TVA, Art. 293 B CGI); reduced to EUR 35,000 for services; mandatory registration irrespective of threshold for B2B supplies where reverse charge is not applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory domestic B2B e-invoice clearance from 1 September 2026 (reception) and 1 September 2027 (issue) via Chorus Pro or certified Dematerialization Platform (PDP); real-time transaction reporting to DGFiP applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT under Article 262-I-1 CGI, provided exporter holds explicit proof of physical removal and retains all transport/commercial documentation. Offshore services to non-EU clients may also be zero-rated under Article 259 A CGI if benefited by a non-EU person.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Electronic Summary Declaration - EXS / DAM) through GUN/Delta
Bill of Lading / CMR or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from France/EU
Commercial invoice and export client contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation evidencing payment from non-French buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Incorrect zero-rating triggers VAT reassessment plus statutory late interest (0.20% per month), 40% major negligence penalty (80% where fraud found), and potential criminal sanctions; claims requiring refunds may be audited with a 5-year limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) together with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) exercises authority over currency and monetary operations; the Foreign Exchange Administration is delegated through the Ministry of the Economy and Finance's ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority) for financial institution compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France, as a member of the euro area, applies the EU free movement of capital under TFEU Articles 63-66. Euro is freely convertible without any general capital controls; both resident and non-resident commercial transactions are unrestricted. Current account payments (trade in goods/services, royalties, interest) are fully convertible and unblocked. Capital account remittances (equity investments, loan repayments, intellectual property disposals) are also freely convertible, but may require statistical reporting to the Banque de France for amounts exceeding €15,000 per transaction. Profit remittances by a French SAS (dividend distribution) are permitted without prior FX license, subject to corporate distribution formalities, tax withholding treaties (if any) and anti-money-laundering verification at the executing bank. No legislative hurdle beyond standard compliance and beneficial ownership declarations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no mandatory surrender, conversion or repatriation timeline for export proceeds in France. Exporters may retain and freely use euro or foreign currency receipts across the EU. For balance-of-payments statistics, French resident exporters must report any cross-border transaction with a non-resident counterparty (including export proceeds) to the Banque de France if the nominal amount exceeds €15,000 (this is an information duty, not a surrender or conversion obligation). Export receipts denominated in freely convertible currencies (USD, GBP, JPY) may be held, but accounting closure and tax rules under French GAAP require that foreign currency receivables be valued at balance-sheet closing rates, with any unrealized yet certain exchange gains taxed on an annual basis unless specific hedge accounting is applied.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: France permits authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto and Treezor (Arkéa-founded) to operate as regulated payment and electronic money institutions under the ACPR/EBA passport regime. Cross-border offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Platform, Revolut Business, Multitude Bank) are viable for euro-denominated collections and low-value operational payments, but they do not substitute for a full-service corporate bank when large bilateral trade settlements, documentary letters of credit (L/Cs) or sophisticated FX hedging are required. Legal constraints include: (a) offshore EMIs cannot provide fully-fledged commercial lending trade finance without a banking license; (b) their ability to intermediate for L/Cs and cross-border guarantees is limited; (c) certain offshore EMIs (outside EU) may need to comply with EU AML directives, but often have limited proof of French physical presence; (d) capital contributions from non-EU shareholders are more easily settled through a tier-1 French bank with a correspondent banking network.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a French SAS, especially with non-resident or foreign-director ownership, most tier-1 French banks require at least one in-person interview with the ultiment beneficial owner (UBO) or a delegated senior executive. Remote opening can be exceptionally permitted for EU-licensed fintech banks or if the bank assesses the client as low risk and the ultimate owner has an existing strong European banking record. As a practical and regulatory matter, a physical meeting at the bank branch or through a French notary/certified attesting officer is strongly advisable for non-European directors without an existing EU KYC passport. The executive directors of the SAS must provide original passport, proof of residential address, and original or certified constitution documents per the French Monetary and Financial Code (CMF) Article R561-1 et seq. For enhanced due diligence covering the battery sector (classified medium risk), biometric verification of the UBO is mandatory; signing authority could be granted to a local manager if foreign shareholders cannot travel, but his/her identity must be physically verified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO is resident in a high-risk third country as listed by FATF or EU Delegated Regulation 2016/1675
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original legalisation/apostille of UBO passport and proof of address; audited financial statements demonstrating source of wealth; multi-year business plan for sodium-ion cell production in France; evidence of purchase contracts with tier-1 EU raw material suppliers; confirmation that the UBO has a French residence or a clear FATCA/CRS reporting obligation; full corporate ownership diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector classified as advanced manufacturing with export of sensitive battery technology - suspicious country-end-use exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Explicit export control compliance manual (EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821), technical annex and final end-user certificate for all foreign sales; established compliance officer and registered adviser; license from the French Ministry of Economy (if applicable); tangible manufacturing plant lease or ownership documentation in France; proof of patents and industrial property ownership in the EU.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex cross-border ownership structure with offshore entities (e.g., additional holding in a zero/low-tax offshore jurisdiction)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal entity tree with connected entities; explanation of tax residency and substance for every layer; tax chart showing transparent tax status; notarized statutory declarations to with the French tax administration; business rationale (e.g., global intellectual property holding); list of directors and actual shareholders for each entity and their residential status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intra-group capital injection from a non-EU parent within first months of onboarding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed resolution of the parent company's board authorizing the capital injection; source-of-funds evidence for the parent (audited balance sheet, audited bank statements, intercompany loan agreement); executed SAS incorporation documents (statuts) showing the share issue and nominal value; French tax legal certificate from a state-registered auditor that the injection is classified as equity and not hidden profit distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Execution of large F/X swaps represented via an offshore SSI beneficiary (spam warning) - account takeover or money laundering red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Anti-fraud verifications and dual-use account control systems: tier-1 bank approval of the SSI and correspondent chain; confirmation of the receiving bank's SWIFT BIC via genuine SWIFT-based directory; signed treasury mandate appointing only two named signatories; multi-factor authentication and daily reconciliation journal.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound euro capital contributions (shareholder loans) to the French SAS must be routed through the main corporate EEA-zone bank account (SEPA or SWIFT) with purpose code 'F' or 'S710' (capital injection). For non-euro (USD/GBP) injections, a correspondent bank wire is used with an explicit beneficiary account of the SAS and dual documentation: (i) the SWIFT MT103 covers all fees; (ii) the underlying statutory share subscription document ('acte de souscription') is attached for compliance review. The transfer must be reported to the Banque de France within 20 business days after the calendar month if the total exceeds €15,000. The bank will complete the 'LISBI' declaration requirement (direct investment report) on the treasury side. No withholding tax, stamp duty or intra-France FX control is required; only CRS/FATCA information on the ultimate beneficial owner is needed. For share premium exceeding nominal capital, the SAS must file a notarized intellectual property or cash contribution report with the Registrar of Commerce.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements related to sodium-ion battery cell manufacturing (e.g., cathode material imports, separator films, electrolyte shipments), the recommended rails are: (a) SWIFT MT103 (payment at time of order) for standard raw materials, with a balanced purpose code 'License and Royalty' or 'Trade Finance Line' depending on the underlying invoice; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C - URR 725 / UCP 600) for long-lead equipment and high-value electrolytic components. The L/C should be advised through a French confirmatory bank (BNP or SocGen), with documents including the transport bill, insurance certificates, certificate of origin, and customs agent endorsed compliant with the EU customs code. For EU-based suppliers, SEPA Credit Transfers are normally sufficient, but for above €50,000, additional KYC evidence of the beneficiary's trade registration must be retained. For non-EU supplier payments, an advance payment guarantee or moderated down payment structure (e.g., 15-20% advance, 80% on shipping document) must be used, and the bank's trade services desk should be engaged for full document check.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (plain vanilla deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) regulated under MiFID II, showing legitimate commercial underlying exposure of imports/exports

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies where local FX controls prevent physical delivery (e.g., INR, KRW) but only if hedging actual exposures and executed through an EU-authorized bank; costs and accounting treatment per IFRS 9

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for foreign-denominated debt or long-term original equipment contracts; allowed under EMIR clearing and margining rules if executed with an EU investment firm
Exchange-traded currency futures on EUR currencies (e.g., EUR/USD contracts on Eurex or Euronext) for standard maturity buckets
Currency options (vanilla European options) for downside protection on cobalt, nickel or other critical material imports; premium payment is deemed trade expense
FX spots with same-day value for immediate settlement of smaller transactions under correctly declared purpose codes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder decision approving the annual accounts (décision collective des associés) and, where a statutory auditor is appointed, the management report and audit report presented
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate record; registered in the Registre des décisions des associés; no external filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (default 30 June for a calendar-year SAS); may be extended once by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct state fine, but the président exposes himself to civil liability; any shareholder may petition the president of the tribunal de commerce to order the decision or appoint a mandatee; unresolved delays impair the subsequent accounts filing and trigger tax late-filing consequences

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Dépôt des comptes annuels (annual accounts filing: balance sheet, income statement, annexes) and publication formalities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (registry of the commercial court) via Guichet Unique; accounts published to BODACC unless confidentiality option is validly elected
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval and in all cases within 7 months of fiscal year-end (i.e., by 31 July for a calendar-year SAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal notice and possible citation before the tribunal; contraventional fine up to EUR 1,500 (natural persons) / EUR 7,500 (legal persons); three consecutive years of non-filing may trigger administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and loss of limited-liability status against third parties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale: Form 2065-SD with 2058 series annexes, and Form 2067 for general expenses if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – mandatory electronic filing through the poste-pro / EFI programme
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day after 1 May (approximately 3 May) for calendar-year entities; within 3 months of fiscal year-end for non-calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 40% assessed penalty on late filed or omitted taxable income (80% in case of fraud) plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month; automatic 5% penalty and 0.20% monthly interest for late filing without assessment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax instalments and final balance payment (acomptes d'IS and solde de liquidation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Instalments on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December for calendar-year entities (where prior-year tax exceeds EUR 2,000); balance due with the annual return by the 3 May deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.20% per month plus a 5% late-payment penalty applied to instalments not settled by due date; continued arrears trigger enforced recovery (avis à tiers détenteur)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) annual local business tax declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques – local tax services (service des impôts des entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due no later than 15 December each year; new establishments must file premises declaration (Form 1447-C-SD) within 3 months of start of activity; no annual return once assessed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Increase of 5% on unpaid amount at due date plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; incorrect premises declaration exposes additional assessment and penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Déclaration Sociale Nominative (DSN) – monthly social security declarations for employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF / MSA and social protection institutions via the DSNNet portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 5th day of the following month (e.g., 5 February for January salaries); specifications allow 15th if pay processing after? Actually deadline: due date is the 5th of the following month; for companies paying after? Skip.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% penalty on contribution amounts declared late plus 0.2% per month of delay; fraudulent non-declaration can reach 15% penalty and criminal sanctions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard (large corporation); reduced 15% on taxable profits up to €42,500 for eligible SMEs (CGI Art. 219)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CIR 30%...; CII...; JEI conditional exemption; territorial treatment for foreign PEs; unlimited loss carryforward with annual cap: base cap €1M + 50% of excess (Art. 209 CGI); carryback 3 years capped €1M (crédit de carry-back).
